_comment: FROZEN GOLDEN QUERY SET — the gate for docs/mcp-migration.md §5 Stage 1.
Every entry is a `recall` shape spoken in BLUE's vocabulary (the kwargs of
remembering/scripts/memory.py::recall). blue.py passes `args` through almost
verbatim; green.mjs translates them onto src/turso.ts's SearchOpts and
declares anything it cannot express. That asymmetry is deliberate: blue is
the specification, so the query set is written in blue's language and green
is measured against it, not the other way round.
FIELDS
id      stable slug. NEVER renumber or reuse — snapshots and CI history
key off it. Add new probes at the end of their group.
why     what divergence this probes. A golden set nobody can interpret
rots into a list of magic strings; if you add a query without a
`why`, you have added noise, not coverage.
args    kwargs for blue's recall(). `raw` and `auto_strengthen` are set by
blue.py and must not appear here.
expect  "parity"   — blue and green MUST agree; a mismatch is a bug.
"known-gap" — green is known not to implement this yet. Still run,
still reported; the gate stays red until it lands or
the entry is demoted. See `gap`.
gap     required when expect is "known-gap": which missing green feature.
ON CORPUS DEPENDENCE
These queries run against the live shared database (§4: data is
single-homed). The absolute result sets therefore change over time — that
is fine and expected, because the harness never asserts on contents. It
asserts that TWO ACCESS PATHS AGREE at the same instant. Search terms were
chosen to be corpus-shaped (turso, mcp, bluesky, perch, boot) so most
probes return rows, and a handful were chosen to return nothing on
purpose — see the `sparse-*` group, which is where the real signal is.

queries.why: Floor case. One term, no filters. If this diverges, nothing below is interpretable — check FTS5 escaping and the composite ORDER BY direction first.
Two terms become an OR of prefix-wildcarded quotes. Probes that both sides build the same MATCH and that BM25 ranks the multi-term hit the same way.
A term expected to match a large slice of the corpus, so the LIMIT bites and ranking — not filtering — decides the answer. This is the purest test of the composite score expression.
FTS5 tokenizing is case-folding, but the escaper preserves the original case inside the quotes. Confirms neither side lower-cases before quoting.
Six terms OR-ed. Probes term-count-dependent BM25 saturation and that neither side truncates or de-duplicates the term list.

args.search: boot payload identity profile ops recent

queries.why: n omitted entirely. Blue defaults to 10 in recall(); green defaults to 10 in buildSearch(). Two independently-written defaults that must not drift apart.

LIMIT 1 compares only the single best-ranked row. Intended as the sharpest test of the ranking expression — it instead caught blue being non-deterministic. Retained, because a query that cannot have a stable answer is worth keeping visible.
queries.gap: BLUE IS NON-DETERMINISTIC HERE, and green is not at fault. n=1 always returns fewer than expansion_threshold (3) rows, so memory.py::recall runs its multi-stage expansion; that loop iterates `for tag in stage1_tags` where stage1_tags is a SET of strings, and breaks early once len(results)+len(expansion_results) >= n*2. With n=1 the cap is 2, so the FIRST tag visited decides the whole answer — and set iteration order over strings is randomised per process by PEP 456 hash randomisation. Measured: recall('bluesky', n=1) returns 8df0ab0d, 889875b9 or 6edc2ff8 depending on PYTHONHASHSEED, and two full blue captures of this 64-query set differ on this entry alone. Green returns the top row by composite score, which is one of blue's possible answers. Do not 'fix' green to match a captured blue id: there is no id to match.

queries.why: At the tool layer's documented cap. Deep result sets expose ranking ties, where SQLite's ordering of equal composite_score rows is unspecified — if this is the ONLY flaky entry, suspect ties, not a port bug.

n=200. turso.ts::search passes n straight to LIMIT, but tools.ts::recall clamps to 50 before calling it. The turso-layer comparison should match blue; green.mjs also records the tool-layer answer so the clamp is visible rather than silent.

LIMIT 0. Both sides should return nothing — but on blue an empty result then trips the expansion stage (0 < expansion_threshold), which re-searches and slices back to [:0]. Confirms expansion cannot resurrect rows past a zero limit.
Single type filter, the most common shape in references/CLAUDE.md. Binds `m.type = ?` as the second parameter on both sides.

recall(type=..., tags=...) with NO search term — SKILL.md line 71. Blue routes this to _query (plain SELECT, ORDER BY t DESC), NOT to FTS5. Green has only the FTS path and will MATCH the literal '""'. Two different queries against two different orderings.
queries.gap: green has no non-FTS _query path; blue falls back to it whenever `search` is falsy

queries.why: A type outside state.TYPES. Neither side validates the filter value, so both should return zero rows — and on blue, zero rows then triggers expansion.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion; blue expands whenever len(results) < expansion_threshold

queries.why: type="". Blue guards with `if type:` so an empty string is IGNORED; green guards with `type !== undefined` so it binds `m.type = ''` and matches nothing. A truthiness-vs-definedness divergence that no unit test would catch.
Two filters composed. Probes that the parameter ORDER (match, type, conf, limit) is identical — a swapped binding is silently wrong, not an error.
One tag, default tag_mode. Blue matches with `m.tags LIKE '%"tag"%' ESCAPE '\'` over the raw JSON text; any port that reaches for json_each returns a different row set.
tag_mode any ORs the clauses inside ONE paren group. If the parens are dropped, the outer AND binds tighter than the OR and unrelated rows leak in.

tag_mode all. Blue appends each tag as its own TOP-LEVEL condition with no wrapping parens, asymmetric with `any`. Semantically identical, textually different — and the harness diffs SQL text upstream of this.

A tag_mode=all pair chosen to be over-constrained, so it returns fewer than 3 rows and pushes blue into expansion while green stops. The intersection of `all` + sparse is where the two engines diverge hardest.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion

queries.why: tags=[]. Blue guards `if tags:`, green guards `tags.length > 0`. Both must skip the clause entirely — an empty tag list must not become an empty paren group, which is a SQL syntax error.

HIGH VALUE. SQLite's LIKE is case-INSENSITIVE for ASCII; `value = ?` under json_each is case-SENSITIVE. Asking for 'Muninn' when the corpus stores 'muninn' returns rows under LIKE and nothing under json_each. This entry is the regression guard for that specific rewrite.
A tag containing '_', which is LIKE's single-character wildcard. Without ESCAPE and escapeLike(), 'boot_mode' also matches 'bootXmode'. Probes that both sides escape the pattern, not just quote it.

A non-ASCII tag. Text LIKE compares the stored bytes, so it depends on whether the JSON was written with escaped \uXXXX or literal UTF-8; json_each would decode first. Probes serialization assumptions, not retrieval.

tags_all= convenience param (SKILL.md line 117). Blue resolves it to tags + tag_mode='all' BEFORE building SQL; green has no such sugar. The harness translates it so this probes the SQL, not the sugar — the sugar gap itself is an API-surface item for §8.
tags_any= convenience param (SKILL.md line 118). Same translation as above; asserts the two sugars land on the two different tag_modes and are not accidentally symmetric.

THE NULL-CONFIDENCE PROBE. Blue emits a bare `m.confidence >= ?`, so a NULL-confidence row fails EVERY threshold. Any port that reuses the ranking expression's COALESCE(m.confidence, 0.5) in the FILTER admits every pre-confidence-era memory at exactly this threshold. 0.5 is where the bug is maximally visible.

conf=0. Blue guards `if conf is not None`, so 0 is APPLIED, and `NULL >= 0` is still NULL — so a conf=0 filter is not a no-op, it is a 'has a confidence value at all' filter. A truthiness guard would drop the clause and return more rows.
Below the 0.5 coalesce default. Distinguishes 'filter ignores NULL' from 'filter coalesces NULL to 0.5': under COALESCE these rows pass, under blue they do not.

Above the coalesce default, where the COALESCE bug is INVISIBLE — both spellings exclude NULLs. Included so a green failure on conf-half plus a green pass here localizes the bug to the coalesce rather than to the comparison.
conf=1.0, the boundary. Probes >= vs > and float equality on the confidence column.

A high threshold on a narrow term, engineered to fall under 3 results. Confidence filtering and expansion interact: blue's expansion stages re-pass `conf` but NOT `session_id`, an asymmetry worth watching.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion

queries.why: Lower time bound alone. Binds `m.t >= ?` — note it filters on `t` (narrative time), not created_at.
Upper bound alone, inclusive. Confirms `<=` not `<`, and that the parameter lands after since's slot even when since is absent.
Both bounds. Probes binding order (since before until) — a swap silently returns nothing for most windows, which reads as 'no data' rather than as a bug.
until < since — an empty window by construction. Guaranteed zero rows, so this is a cheap deterministic expansion trigger that does not depend on the corpus at all.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion

queries.why: HIGH VALUE. A timestamp with a +02:00 offset. Blue runs since/until through result.py::normalize_to_utc before binding; green binds the raw string. The DB stores Z-suffixed UTC, so green's comparison is a LEXICOGRAPHIC compare against a differently-formatted string — off by the offset, or matching nothing.
queries.gap: green does not call normalize_to_utc on since/until

queries.why: '2026-03-01' with no time and no zone — the shape SKILL.md line 113 actually documents. Blue normalizes it; green binds it bare, and '2026-03-01' < '2026-03-01T00:00:00Z' lexicographically, so the two windows differ at the boundary day.
queries.gap: green does not call normalize_to_utc on since/until

queries.why: Session scoping (advanced-operations.md line 328). Binds `m.session_id = ?`. Sessions are narrow, so this usually also lands under the expansion threshold — read it together with its result count.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion; blue's expansion stages also DROP session_id, so blue can return cross-session rows here

queries.why: A session that cannot exist. Deterministic zero-row filter, so it isolates expansion behaviour from corpus drift. On blue watch for rows coming back ANYWAY — the expansion stages do not re-pass session_id.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion; blue's expansion stages drop session_id and can leak other sessions' rows

queries.why: session_id composed with type and tags, to pin the full parameter binding order: match, type, tags..., conf, session_id, since, until, limit.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion

queries.why: episodic=True adds `* (1.0 + ln(1.0 + COALESCE(m.access_count, 0)) * 0.2)` to the composite. THE ORDER-SENSITIVE PROBE: it is the only ranking input the harness itself perturbs, because reading is not free. Capture blue and green close together or this reorders under you.

episodic=False stated rather than defaulted. The non-episodic composite must contain no reference to access_count at all — a boost multiplied by ln(1+0)=0 is not the same as an absent boost if the column is NULL.

Episodic ranking on a query that returns under 3 rows: blue applies the access boost, then throws the ordering away and re-sorts by expansion boost_scores instead. Documents that expansion OVERRIDES episodic ranking on blue.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion

queries.why: A token that cannot appear in the corpus. Zero primary hits sends blue down the 'no stage1 tags' branch, which expands the QUERY WORDS via _cooccurrence_expand at min_pmi=0.0 and can return rows from nowhere. Green returns nothing. The single loudest expected divergence in the set.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion

queries.why: Two rare-but-real terms. Expected 1-2 primary hits, which is the interesting case: blue KEEPS them and then appends expansion rows, so blue's list starts like green's and then continues. Diff should classify this as EXTRA, not SET-DIFF.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion

queries.why: THE CONTROL. Same sparse shape as sparse-rare-compound but expansion_threshold=0 disables blue's expansion entirely. This is the ONE sparse entry that must be exact parity today — if it fails, the divergence is in retrieval, not in the missing expansion stage.
expansion_threshold=10 on a query returning ~5 rows, so expansion fires where it normally would not. Confirms the threshold is a comparison against the PRIMARY result count, not against n.
queries.gap: green has no multi-stage expansion

queries.why: A near-unique term with expansion off. Isolates 'does green find the same one row' from 'does green invent the other nine', which the enabled variants conflate.

search="". Blue's `if search and not strict` is FALSY, so it never reaches FTS at all — it runs _query, a plain SELECT ordered by t DESC. Green escapes to the literal '""' and runs it as a MATCH. Same call, two entirely different queries and two different orderings.
queries.gap: green has no non-FTS _query path for falsy search

queries.why: search="   ". Truthy in Python, so blue DOES reach FTS and escapes to '""' — unlike empty-string above. The two adjacent entries pin exactly where blue's routing boundary sits.
Whitespace that is not spaces. Python's str.split() with no argument splits on ALL whitespace; a port that splits on ' ' alone produces empty terms and a malformed MATCH.

recall(n=50) with no search at all — SKILL.md line 215, a real and common shape. search defaults to None, so blue goes to _query with no text predicate: the newest 50 memories. Green has no such path.
queries.gap: green has no non-FTS _query path; there is no MCP equivalent of 'just give me the newest N'

queries.why: A double quote inside the query. FTS5 special chars become SPACES, not escapes, so 'say "hi"' splits into two terms. Pinned by fts-golden.json vector 6 — this entry proves the vector survives contact with a real MATCH.
'a*b' becomes two terms, not the concatenation 'ab'. Replacing specials with '' instead of ' ' is the single most tempting simplification of the escaper and it changes results silently.
Every FTS5 special char in one string: " * ( ) : ^. Exercises the whole replacement table in one pass against a live MATCH rather than against a string assertion.
'foo AND bar' — the operator must be STRIPPED, not honoured, or a user query can restructure the MATCH into an intersection. Both sides should search foo OR bar.
Keywords are compared UPPERCASED, so a lowercase 'and' is stripped too. Probes that the case-folding happens on the comparison and not on the emitted term.

'AND OR NOT NEAR' strips to nothing, and an empty MATCH is an FTS5 SYNTAX ERROR — which is why both sides must emit the literal '""'. If one side emits an empty string this is the entry that throws instead of returning rows.
NEAR is stripped like the boolean operators, leaving a bare two-term OR. Included separately because NEAR takes a different argument shape in FTS5 and is easy to forget in the keyword set.

A hyphenated token and a non-ASCII token. Hyphen is NOT in the special set, so 'turso-libsql' stays one quoted term while the tokenizer may still split it — a place where escaping and tokenizing disagree.
strict=True skips FTS and ranking entirely: blue runs `summary LIKE '%term%'` ordered by t DESC. Substring matching, not tokenized matching — 'call' matches 'recall'. Green has no strict mode.
queries.gap: green implements no strict/LIKE path

queries.why: fetch_all=True is the documented way to get everything (SKILL.md line 110); blue nulls out search and falls to _query. Green has no equivalent, and adding one has a real tool-budget cost (§2) — this entry is the evidence for that decision.
queries.gap: green implements no fetch_all path

queries.why: exploration=True reranks CLIENT-SIDE in Python — 1/(1+access_count) added to an inverse-rank proxy — so it is the one ranking behaviour that is NOT server-side SQL and therefore not free to port. Expect a different order even once green's SQL matches.
queries.gap: green implements no exploration rerank; unlike the rest of ranking this one is application code, not SQL

queries.why: recall("*") RAISES ValueError on blue by design (SKILL.md line 121) to push callers to fetch_all. Green happily escapes '*' to '""' and returns rows. An error-on-one-side-only case, and a reminder that parity includes parity of refusals.
queries.gap: green does not implement blue's wildcard guard; it returns results where blue refuses
